ateret-zekenim/4:_: It is the first place in each of the first verses of the earth that is not repeated and swayed in the bread of the earth, and it is not possible for the first time, and it is not because of it, it is not possible that it is not possible for it, and it is not because of it
ateret-zekenim/7:_: In the knife of Kush and R. D.D., the knife must be prohibited if he is cut off in the Passover because he is a strong thing as a “J.D.” for the matter of the Chun
biur-halacha/1:ב: And likewise if it touched etc. — at first glance this has no explanation, namely this; and I found in Mateh Yehudah who forced an explanation and wrote that one can say: since in other prohibitions in Yoreh De'ah siman 105 only touching of roasting is mentioned — the way they roasted with its fat or a piece that was roasted with the forbidden substance — and heat of its surface is not mentioned there, therefore he wrote "and likewise if chametz bread touched" etc., meaning: in the first clause, heat of its roasting, and in the second clause heat of its surface — in both only the place of contact is forbidden. And know that heat of its roasting here means there is only touching alone; but that which is below siman 467 subsection 15, that there are those who forbid the entire thing, deals with roasting by a spit, for when one turns the spit the taste spreads through the entire thing, as explained there — end of his words. And in my humble opinion it appears it should read "and therefore."
biur-halacha/1:ג: And there is no permeating substance etc. alone — see Magen Avraham in subsection 2 at its end, who wrote that the law of its surface is like roasting; nevertheless it appears to me one should rule here as Rama wrote in salting in siman 467 seif 14, that in any case roasting is not better than salting; and see in Peri Megadim who wrote that although the Rav was silent here on what the Mechaber wrote "there is no permeating substance, only the place of contact is forbidden," I do not agree except he relied on 467 seif 14 regarding salting, that they forbid that entire piece b'eyna in sixty, and on Pesach in any amount; and in truth such is Bach's view there in siman 461. In practice one should look, for Peri Chadash below in siman 461 and Gra in this siman and Maamar Mordechai in siman 461 — all their view is to be lenient like Shulchan Aruch's ruling; and therefore their reason is specifically in salting, where the forbidden substance is found on the meat, where sometimes it is fatty [and also because we do not know at which place the contact was, therefore they are stringent on that piece]; not so in our matter with two loaves where fattiness does not apply at all — one need not be stringent. However Eshel Avraham's view is like Bach, and I found several other Acharonim who copied Bach's words; and all this is only because of the stringency of chametz — people are accustomed to be stringent; and it appears that in a place of loss one may rely to be lenient in this. Afterwards I found in Yoreh De'ah siman 105 in Peri Megadim in Sha'ar HaTevunah section 38 who also sides to be lenient in a place of loss regarding a weak forbidden substance that has no fattiness at all.
biur-halacha/1:ה: Where reicha applies — see Mishna Berurah in what he wrote "but in a thing where the name reicha does not apply" etc.; and regarding cooking see Magen Avraham who concludes that what the Rav was stringent about in Yoreh De'ah siman 108 seif 2 in the gloss regarding when the oven was completely sealed, even in cooking [unless in great loss], deals specifically with hot foods insulated for Shabbat, for since they remain a long time inside the oven and the oven is sealed on every side, their smell is strong and its law is like roasting; but in ordinary cooking, even if they remain an hour or two, one need not be stringent. And regarding Pesach see what is written in Mishna Berurah.
biur-halacha/4:ג: Wet — see in Chemed Moshe who proved that what Rama wrote wet in wet is not precise that both were wet, but if only the chametz was wet, even if the permitted substance is dry, it also does not revive — see there.
biur-halacha/5:א: It is permitted to eat at the time that the author is allowed to remove him from the salt, only to the extent of the author’s consciousness, to remove him even from the Passover and the Rambam, to remove him from the past:
biur-halacha/5:ב: In the water and so on, but if they were not in the water, they were dry in the palm of the veins, they were not fed with dry rods, and even from time to time in the palm of the horn, they were occupied as “a thing for bread and diving.”
biur-halacha/5:ג: The flesh of the D.P., look at the mouth of the D.C., which has been circulated in the name of the D.A. every day, but all the lasts do not remember this and the Gra means that DDT is another one day. And Dr. Hubbard wrote the world to say a sermon that was six hours, but in retrospect, it is better than impeachment
biur-halacha/5:ד: Even in the evening of the night
biur-halacha/5:ה: Forbidden by law if they were not careful etc. and that they did not melt etc. — see Magen Avraham subsection 21 who explains Rama's words that it is not permitted by law unless they were careful in both matters; and explanation is needed, for in cheeses he was not concerned b'dieved about chametz crumbs, only to be stringent l'chatchila; and I saw in Mateh Yehudah who elaborated on this, and his view is that Rama's main point that it is forbidden by law is only because of concern for discharge from chametz vessels, and he forced Rama's language greatly — see there; and in my humble opinion Rama was stringent only regarding fat, b'dieved because of chametz crumbs, similar to what Chok Yaakov wrote in subsection 30 in the name of Mahari"t that it is customary to gather etc. — see there; and therefore crumbs of chametz are found in it; but in other things Rama truly mentioned only concern for chametz vessels, and so is proven in Darkei Moshe that preserves are permitted if made in the designated vessel, and he wrote explicitly that because of chametz crumbs we are not concerned; and so Acharonim copied stam; and also from Magen Avraham in subsection 26 it is implied only in fat we are concerned for crumbs even b'dieved, not in cooked wine and the like — see there; however from Chok Yaakov in subsection 33 it is implied he does not distinguish in this; and see in Shulchan Aruch of Gra section 47, and this requires study.
biur-halacha/5:ו: And likewise anything etc. — know that there are Poskim who hold specifically regarding fat, that the pan in which they melt it is customarily used constantly, and likewise similar cases regarding pots used frequently — presumably they are ben yomo until you know they are not ben yomo; but in other vessels we say presumably they are not ben yomo [and this is Mahari"t's view, agreed by Kenesset HaGedolah and Peri Chadash]; nevertheless from Shulchan Aruch and Acharonim it is implied that because of chametz stringency we are stringent in every case. And regarding mixtures, Magen Avraham's view in subsection 26 is to be lenient in wine and vinegar except fat because crumbs do not usually mix into them, even if they became mixed in less than sixty; and Chok Yaakov's view in subsection 32 implies in all things one is not lenient except in great loss; and it appears one may rely on Magen Avraham's view since Mahari"t and his supporters are lenient in stam vessels even without mixtures; and likewise in fat one may rely on Chok Yaakov to be lenient in great loss, for several Acharonim copied his words for halachah [Gra and Magen Alef and Makor Chayim]; and also implied in Gra's explanation there that the essential law is stringency — see there.
biur-halacha/5:ז: That they cook in chametz vessels etc. — see in Beit Meir who elaborated and wrote that he means at least it is known that it was cooked, even if there is doubt whether it was a chametz vessel — we presume all vessels stam are chametz vessels if it is not known they have designated vessels; but if there is doubt whether it was cooked at all, such as the herb called tea — what prohibition concern is there; and I heard people say the reason is perhaps it is counterfeit, what was already determined boiled and dried; but in this both reasons of Rabbenu Tam (brought in Beit Yosef) apply — from where do we presume prohibition, and also we taste it all year etc.; and in this there is no concern the counterfeit was made on Pesach and there is any amount in it, for it comes from a distant land; and why not say everything separated from the majority is separated — see there where he elaborated and concludes in my humble opinion it is only like things permitted and others practiced prohibition by mistake.
biur-halacha/5:ח: But on the last good day, it should be eased – and the dust of Dachman doubts the bulk of Kulai Daxilin in this last bioteger, I have declined to disdain:
biur-halacha/6:_: A salt named in the cry - and Dukk in the cry, but a salt that is put in other tools that are accustomed to use them a lot of vines should not be used on Passover. The Last:
biur-halacha/7:_: Unripe grapes crushed before Pesach — from this wording it is implied that during Pesach one may not be lenient; and the reason is because of what Semak concluded at the end of his words "and even if it discharges" etc. [as brought by Taz]; therefore according to this it is permitted only before Pesach, and Rama decided for practical law like the first part of his words that it does not discharge when cold, and therefore even during Pesach it is permitted [Mordechai]; however it is difficult, for Rama should have written "and some say" or "it appears to me," not stam; and Mateh Yehudah already challenged this and it remains in difficulty; and in my humble opinion if we hold for practical law like Eshel Avraham and Netziv that before Pesach it is permitted when crushed even if the mortar was not clean — it is simple the Mechaber deals when the vessel was not clean, and therefore they permit only before Pesach; and Rama's language fits very well for one who examines and understands.
biur-halacha/11:_: Whether chametz etc. — see Mishna Berurah where I wrote: if it became mixed in less than sixty etc. — according to his view, through chametz mixtures of a kezayit, so it is in the beginning of siman 442 in Magen Avraham — see there: if there is not sixty against a kezayit, according to all one does not transgress bal yera'eh; and so Gra brought in this siman; and I did not copy what Magen Avraham brought in the name of Bach, that if it became mixed in less than sixty, even if there was not a kezayit, one does not transgress bal yera'eh, nevertheless for eating it is forbidden after Pesach because chametz taste in pieces is forbidden without redemption, because Beit Meir questioned this since one did not transgress bal yera'eh on this mixture, why should it not be permitted in eating (and taste of chametz in pieces does not apply after Pesach); and so implied in Gra's explanation in subsection 39 that the Mechaber who requires sixty deals when there is at least a kezayit; and in subsection 41 it is implied that regarding mixtures on which one did not transgress bal yera'eh, it is permitted in eating and benefit, even without redemption — and this is even without redemption that the Mechaber does not deal with this; however Makor Chayim's view here is like Magen Avraham, that even less than a kezayit is forbidden without redemption, and his reason is because many Poskim hold one transgresses bal yera'eh also on less than a kezayit; and perhaps Gra also holds one transgresses bal yera'eh even on less than a kezayit, but this is specifically when it is b'eyna and not through mixtures — and this requires study for practical law.
chatam-sofer/1:_: In the Mechaber seif 1 in the gloss — Mordechai, perek Kol Sha'ah, and there are those who are stringent; see Mishna Berurah siman 570 there, and what Magen Avraham subsection 4 wrote regarding his name, and this requires clarification.
chatam-sofer/3:_: (There in Magen Avraham subsection 3) And so too in the responsum of Maharil — see there; the Maharil in the responsum there, and proof that one does not permit meat of a slaughtered animal with nevelah in any case, even when both are one species, even according to those who hold min b'mino in any amount; and so it is proven in the chapter Keitzad Tzolin, for they challenge according to those who hold because of mixed flavors: what difference to me between kid and kid, what difference between kid and lamb — let us say that not only kid and kid, which is min b'mino, etc.; and according to R' Yehuda and Rabbi who ordered the mishnah it is min b'mino in any amount, etc. And with this he corrected the words of Magen Avraham subsection 4, and this requires clarification.
chatam-sofer/5:_: (There in Magen Avraham subsection 4) Unless in a place where Tosafot disagree — see there; we are concerned to be stringent, and so too Mahariik at the beginning of shoresh — see there.
chatam-sofer/6:_: (There in Magen Avraham subsection 6) And Mordechai chapter 2 etc. regarding wheat — see there; Chok Yaakov challenged this with correct words, and regarding wheat he wrote to see below siman 467 seif 12. And I saw an incident in Pappenheim where the sages of the city forbade well water into which barley fell, even to bake from them before Pesach.
chatam-sofer/8:_: (There in Magen Avraham subsection 16) Regarding absorption of notar — see there; the explanation is: since we find regarding kodshim a Torah decree, the Sages forbade in non-sacred meat as well; and see Tosafot Zevachim daf 96a, s.v. ve'im tash etc.
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 5 in the gloss: but in fat, if one melted it in a chametz vessel it is forbidden by law if they were not careful at the time of making it from chametz etc. — see there; but if they were careful, only with a different intent — not for the sake of Pesach — see Chok Yaakov in the name of Tzitz Eliezer, and see in my compositions on Yoreh De'ah, year 5596, siman 23, to the community of Karitz, what he wrote there as proof from Mishnah chapter 3 of Parah — see there and understand.
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: (There seif 12) chametz nokshah, even b'eyna, is not forbidden in benefit. — see there; see in Magen Avraham until "there is concern that each person will do so" etc. — it is implied that otherwise it would be permitted in benefit; and see in Shitah Mekubetzet in Bava Kamma chapter 9 daf 96b in the mishnah regarding one who stole chametz and Pesach passed over it, he says to him "here is yours before you," for he wrote in the name of Rambam Scarti that neither the robber nor the robbed transgress bal yera'eh — see there. And this is wondrous, for if so why is it forbidden in benefit, and if permitted what does it teach — it is obvious he can return it, and this requires study; and see in my compositions on Bava Kamma daf 98b where I settled this, with God's help — see there and understand.
dagul-merevavah/1:_: His words require study, for even in that same chicken the Shulchan Aruch wrote the reason there because of turning the spit, and there certainly there is a difference between a weak chicken and a fat one, as Magen Avraham wrote there in siman 467 subsection 34.
dagul-merevavah/2:_: Instead of a loss to allow us to rise even though not in place of loss and precision:
dagul-merevavah/4:_: Not a second-new Annanohu, then, as a olive, is permitted to stay, but to what he said, it is forbidden to drink a tear to his stay as permitted as the “Gray” on it concludes that if there is an olive in one place, it must be sorrowful and perhaps if we were done in the dark:
dagul-merevavah/5:_: And see in the Ran who compared it to terumot, etc., and see in Yoreh De'ah siman 323 in Tur and Beit Yosef.
dagul-merevavah/6:_: His intent is that dry in dry revives, and according to this what Beit Yosef wrote in siman 447 that Rabbeinu Yerucham wrote in the name of Rashba that it revives on Pesach must mean only dry in dry; but wet in wet certainly according to Rashba it does not revive, for otherwise why need he say it is like nullifying a prohibition, and this requires clarification.
dagul-merevavah/7:_: It appears to me that even though it is still permitted, nevertheless chametz whose name is upon it is like nullifying a prohibition.
dagul-merevavah/8:_: Dr. Nar prohibits the milk of a rash whose name is on it and leaves the milk in the tummy, and what I wrote above
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: (1) In any amount, etc. And regarding if a prohibition forbidden in any amount became mixed into another dish — Taz elaborated in Yoreh De'ah siman 92 and concludes: when a piece was forbidden in any amount and returned and fell into another and they removed it, its discharge does not forbid in any amount; but moist in moist mixed this way is forever forbidden in any amount — end of his words. In Nikudat HaKesef he elaborated to distinguish — it is wondrous: all decisors forbid, for anyway that minute taste mixed with another force is not its kind relative to other pieces though mixed, but on Pesach forbidden in any amount even not in its kind — end briefly. In my humble opinion it is greatly strained to explain this as not in its kind since all is one meat species; I looked in Tosafot Chullin daf 100 s.v. keshekadim and found per my opinion proven from what Tosafot wrote in the name of Rabbenu Ephraim: in any case we say a piece became nevelah — meaning the permitted became forbidden; if so in other prohibitions the permitted does not become like forbidden at all; and since the prohibition does not impart taste in the piece it has no power to spread — therefore Rabbenu Ephraim explained we say a piece became nevelah only in meat and milk; if so in other prohibitions there is no "piece became nevelah"; and when it does not impart taste, e.g. there are sixty in the piece, Chazal were not stringent to say piece became nevelah — wanted to say the permitted becomes like actual prohibition; if so the prohibition is only due to minute amount and that minute amount has no power to spread — so appears clear in Tosafot's explanation; and so in Rashba daf 101b and Mishmeret HaBayit daf 94 and Terumat HaDeshen siman 51 and Rosh; and what he relied on in Ran end of perek Gid HaNasheh — even in min b'mino not nullified — we did not hear so; rather my explanation: R' Yehuda was stringent only on actual prohibition minute amount mixed; but if before mixing there is also permitted taste it is not so severe that it should not be nullified — and that is how Ran explained and wrote "another taste of permitted" — end; and if so all the more on Pesach where prohibition in any amount is only rabbinic; and further it appears from Ran's opening "they strained and answered" — therefore I wrote Tosafot's answer seems correct to me and all great ones wrote Tosafot's answer and so we hold. What Nikudat HaKesef wondered on Taz — why only if it fell into another and they removed it; even if they did not remove it does it not forbid other pieces — he elaborated scribal error — end. In my opinion Taz's words as plain meaning: excluding if one does not recognize the piece — then since the piece itself is forbidden as Tosafot there, and moist forbids only the first piece, etc., all forbidden for no nullification on Pesach even dry in dry; and so I proved in Eliyahu Zuta from Tosafot and Rosh at length; I also wondered there on Rosh Avodah Zarah — not written here except what touches halachah. What Nikudat HaKesef wrote from siman 467 note 12 that Rama wrote if mixed with others be lenient from doubt — seems not proof; one may say when the second dish lacks majority against the pieces; or Rama refers to mixture moist in moist — we permit on rabbinic doubt; and even if Rama holds so, nevertheless I proved above Tosafot and great Poskim to permit; Taz strengthened his words in Orach Chayim and wrote a peg so it will not move. Conclusion: be lenient when a piece forbidden in any amount fell into another dish with majority against it when they recognize the piece and removed it; but if not recognized all forbidden; and a spoon absorbing from minute amount forbids in any amount:
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: I don't need six or so. It is purely salty and unclean that the Passover should be allowed in place of loss (Haqqah Jacob), see the opinion of Section 1 and the sign of the S.C
eliyah-rabbah/5:_: (5) What bubbles, etc. — implies if something bubbles even if the prohibition is weak, the permitted seasons it; so with matzot smeared with oil — if touched where not folded it is permitted for absorbed prohibition does not emerge, etc. (Magen Avraham); Chok Yaakov challenged — this is not called absorbed prohibition since on this matzah the prohibition exists independently — end; and I say this reasoning is explicit in Rashal I brought in siman 464 note 16 that it is absorbed prohibition. What Magen Avraham wrote agrees with Rashal's explanation and Shach's explanation in Yoreh De'ah siman 105 note 18; but Darkei Moshe's explanation that in fully weak absorbed prohibition we do not say the permitted seasons it is difficult from here — chametz is fully weak and nevertheless he wrote where nothing bubbles; Chok Yaakov answered he holds specifically there in salting there is a distinction in fully weak unlike hot — end; and I challenged him: there in Yoreh De'ah explicitly in what was roasted together and even so permits in fully weak; in my opinion Darkei Moshe explains what he wrote here "where nothing bubbles" — gravy; also in what Taz wrote hot without gravy in meat, etc., no difficulty — not about chametz; nevertheless in my book on Yoreh De'ah I challenged much anyway on Darkei Moshe; therefore primarily like Magen Avraham; greater: Magen Avraham in siman 461 note 12 forbids even touched on one side — and so his conclusion since he concluded like Rama in siman 467 seif 14 in salting — end; and it appears to me to be lenient on folded matzah since early Poskim did not mention such stringency as in siman 461:
eliyah-rabbah/6:_: [and] the place of touch and so on. And if we cook without a recent piece of opinion in the rest of the prohibition against the shell, and if I do see it in the Passover, it is forbidden to something, and it is written by the defense of Avraham at the end of the sign of the Holy One, though I have raised this sign, that I do not prohibit any other dish from being cursed, that I have not taken any of my body against the evil and cannot be as a result of it
eliyah-rabbah/8:_: (8) [Levush] In sixty, etc. — implies he holds chametz is not davar sheyesh lo matirin and therefore nullified in sixty even in its kind; so Torat Chatat klal 36 and Sefer Api Ravrevi; and not like Taz and Shach in Yoreh De'ah end siman 102 — there I clarified; and so in Shulchan Gevura perek HaSho'el:
eliyah-rabbah/9:_: (9) Taste for detriment, etc. Se'or or chametz cooked with cooked or roasted meat imparts taste for detriment (Magen Avraham in Shibolei Leket); Chok Yaakov wondered what detriment applies; see Yam Shel Shlomo — he wrote explicitly: se'or or chametz fell into a pot or cooked with roasted meat — one knows immediately it imparts taste for detriment in that food and permitted, etc. — end; I looked at what he wrote "one knows" not "and one knows" — so in Sefer Tanya siman 46 — implies we know from stam that it is so; and so at the end of his words. Magen Avraham wrote wheat in a well is taste for detriment; Chok Yaakov wrote this is not clear as he wrote siman 467 note 12 — end; in my opinion there it refers to wheat in water in a vessel not a well. Magen Avraham wrote barley in a pit is taste for detriment; chametz dough in a well is taste for detriment:
eliyah-rabbah/10:_: (10) [Levush] Intentionally, etc. — implies even with sixty forbidden intentionally for it refers to siman 4; and study needed in note 11 he wrote even l'chatchila one may mix and retain; Tur not difficult — possibly Tur holds even if mixed automatically forbidden; and truly for Tur even automatically forbidden in this; and though without sixty implies forbidden in benefit after Pesach — one may say he relied on his teacher to permit benefit since the bread was crushed; but on Levush study needed; I again looked in Rabbenu Yerucham daf 46a — implies also with sixty and still must burn before Pesach for it is intentional since one must act with chametz; end; Magen Avraham beginning siman 442 implies there even to mix intentionally to retain forbidden — end; meaning because one must act with it it is called intentional; and therefore in something one need not act perhaps permitted l'chatchila in sixty to retain — so explain Levush and Tur; and so resolve Levush's question; and so Taz; and study needed; further one may say what he permits below refers when already mixed but lacking sixty permitted to mix more; but here the teacher refers to chametz b'eyna forbidden to mix — study needed; greater: Taz wrote moist mixed permitted to mix in sixty even to eat on Pesach — brought proof from Sukkah siman 466 — also requires study for responsum of Rashba siman 491 clearly forbidden as nullifying prohibition; incidentally I note what Magen Avraham siman 442 note 13 wondered on Rosh beginning perek Kol Sha'ah on almori — seems even per second view permitted in benefit; what do they argue with first view; therefore explained second view forbids benefit agreeing with Rosh; wondered on Tur permitting — see there; I found in Rabbenu Yerucham daf 45 — one view: chametz over which Pesach passed permitted in benefit; via mixture permitted in eating; most Poskim forbade; end; undoubtedly his words from Rosh; no doubt this version was before Tur; if so even forbidders appear permitted in benefit:
eliyah-rabbah/11:_: (11) [Levush] And they impart taste, etc. — meaning whether by heating or by pickling; per those who say in cold it imparts taste even without pickling — forbidden; and implies whatever does not impart taste even with substance there does not revive; so Olat Shabbat; and even per those who say it revives — implies forbidden even without imparting taste like dry in dry mixed before Pesach; from Levush and Rama those who say no revival permit when no taste and we rule like them; so responsum of Rashba siman 485 regarding dry in dry — for Geonim forbidden, etc.; implies for those who say no revival permitted also here; see there; and so She'erit Kenesset HaGedolah; if so dry in dry nullified one in two before Pesach — whenever they do not cook on Pesach there is no prohibition; per this what Rama wrote on dry mixed also refers when it imparts taste on Pesach; and rely on end of his words; and not like Magen Avraham who forbade even to retain and understood Rama's dry, etc.; in my opinion as I explained; perhaps therefore Levush omitted dry; but not necessary — examine:
eliyah-rabbah/12:_: It is forbidden and forbidden. But it is permissible to hold and receive pleasure, and see the sign of the KC:
eshel-avraham/1:א: In any amount. And see in responsa Yoreh De'ah siman 563 where there is a doubt of mixtures, all agree it is permitted, for it is a doubt in a rabbinic matter — perhaps it did not mix, and perhaps the law is according to those who hold it is nullified. And know what the Mechaber wrote "in any amount" — for in sixty he permits selling the chicken outside etc. Rather, less than sixty: because it is a davar sheyesh lo matirin. And see Yoreh De'ah siman 102 where he wrote in the name of Rashba that chametz is not in this category, which spoils while waiting. And for this reason Rambam was precise; but in bread that is not lost while waiting — see there. And according to Rosh who were stringent regarding it, whether because of the stringency of bal yera'eh or because it returns to prohibition next year — even in a dish that spoils it is forbidden even in any amount.
eshel-avraham/2:_: Oh, my sister. Dr. Kedara snaked from a cave before, and because of it, he mistakenly called Moses C.C
eshel-avraham/4:א: Not returning. Even the wise men were not allowed before the Passover, but rather, they were told that they would not be the house of Judah
eshel-avraham/4:ב: In a dry thing. Two loaves of chametz mixed with several loaves of matzah — Chok Yaakov and Peri Chadash raised that b'eyna their law is like other prohibitions and one in two is nullified. And in responsa Devar Moshe siman 26 he raised that if they are not yet baked it is nullified, but not after baking, for it is a significant item — see there at length for laws branching from this.
eshel-avraham/5:_: And in karpas. See explained well what he wrote in the name of Magen Avraham, and from this R' Mendel wanted to forbid even to retain them. And in responsa Shev Yaakov 19 he learned advocacy for the custom of Israel that we are not at all strict to sell them on Pesach, even those made with garlic cut with a chametz knife — from that which is in the gloss itself: "and likewise if a minute amount of these things became mixed" etc., that one need not be stringent in the mixture — see there. And Magen Avraham wrote the reason is ta'am bar ta'am, and also perhaps the vessel was not ben yomo. Nevertheless this requires study, for in any case one may rely b'dieved on stam vessels that are not ben yomo and ta'am bar ta'am etc., and he concludes that what Rama wrote "if a minute amount became mixed" is only regarding fat, for when much became mixed it is certainly forbidden because of concern for chametz crumbs inside; but cooked wine etc. — see there. It turns out that even if there are not sixty against the chametz in the vessel in which it was cooked, it is permitted because it mixed on Pesach, since stam vessels are not ben yomo and it is ta'am bar ta'am — automatically they are permitted to retain, for after all prohibition in any amount even in ben yomo is lighter than a vessel that is not ben yomo and where there are not sixty against the prohibition — see Yoreh De'ah siman 99 and siman 102 seif 5; and even though Taz there argues to be stringent, nevertheless at least the reasoning is clear, and if so since ta'am bar ta'am in not ben yomo even without sixty against prohibition is permitted, all the more so in any amount even in ben yomo where it is ta'am bar ta'am, permitted on the last day of Pesach, and likewise to retain them. And one could say that its sharpness neutralizes chametz taste; nevertheless regarding absorption it is only any amount — see Tosafot Pesachim. And even though we hold stam knives have fat smeared on their surface, nevertheless chametz is not usually on the surface; and see in Darkei Moshe what he wrote in the name of responsum of Rosh regarding an onion cut with a knife that he was not concerned at all that chametz was smeared on the surface; and Magen Avraham subsection 37. And furthermore otherwise there is reason for the custom because many Poskim hold that garlic and the like are not called a sharp thing — see Yoreh De'ah at the beginning of siman 96; and there is at least room to rely on them and retain it, especially regarding rabbinic prohibition in any amount — see there.

biur-halacha/1:ד: And there are those who are stringent etc. — Mateh Yehudah wrote: it appears one should be stringent only in something uncommon, for example if chametz bread was baked on Pesach with fatty meat — in this one should be stringent, because although it is not a common thing in any amount, nevertheless there is a concern; but in something common, such as wheat found in one of the dishes in an oven, there is no reason to be stringent even in a completely sealed oven where reicha applies, for this is less than two rabbinic any-amounts that the Acharonim spoke of — for even from actual fatty meat it is not [according to what we hold fully absorbed] except any amount, and this smell coming from the wheat, even if its entire body became mixed, is only any amount and through smell; and according to Yerushalmi and Ramban to Levi, in truth even any amount is not certain in such a case — it is not worth relying on the question to permit, especially in a place preventing Yom Tov joy; and there is no proof from Tosafot who are stringent even regarding wheat, for they rule like Rav that reicha is a matter; etc. — see there where he elaborated and concludes thus for practical law.

biur-halacha/2:ג: Also permitted. Shibolei Leket wrote: chametz or chametz that fell into a pot or was cooked with roasted meat — it gives taste for detriment and is permitted, end of his words. And it is implied from his language that he was precise to write cooked with roasted meat, but with cooked meat it is not for detriment [and not like Magen Avraham implies that he does not distinguish in this]; and even if it fell into a dish, not in every dough that fell into a dish do we say it is for detriment, but in something very sour that is not customary to put in a dish — in this we say it is presumably spoiled [and with this the difficulty of Beit HaTovim from Yoreh De'ah siman 323 is resolved, where it says if dough of challah fell into a dish it forbids]. And see Chok Yaakov who challenged Magen Avraham, and Rabbi Akiva Eiger resolved it that presumably here too it is for detriment; and according to what we explained, Shibolei Leket's intent is not in every chametz, but in that which is very sour. And perhaps he too agrees in this for practical law. And regarding grain kernels found in a well of water on Pesach whether this is called taste for detriment, see Magen Avraham and Rabbi Akiva Eiger and Peri Megadim, and it will be explained below in siman 467 seif 13. And regarding dough of chametz that fell into a well see below siman 467 seif 12 in Mishna Berurah s.v. ein.
biur-halacha/5:ט: He must destroy it — and regarding wine whether it is permitted to drink it, at first glance the matter is simple that before two months when it already dried and does not give taste in wine, one pours the wine from the barrel and it is permitted to drink, and all the more to retain; and if within two months when it gives taste in wine that Rama forbade drinking — regarding retaining it depends on the two resolutions in Magen Avraham subsection 30: Per the first resolution it is forbidden, Per the second permitted; and it appears the second resolution is primary.
biur-halacha/8:א: If it is not ben yomo etc. — see Mishna Berurah that if it is ben yomo it is forbidden, and so in Tur; and see Rabbi Akiva Eiger and other Acharonim who noted that through pickling it is never ben yomo, for the absorption of the forbidden substance or chametz is completed before the absorption of the pickled item placed afterward; and so Magen Avraham above in seif 5 wrote there that it cannot be conceived to forbid through pickling except when it was b'eyna — at the moment they removed the chametz at that moment they placed the pickled item, and this is forced, for then Tur and Mechaber should have explained and not been stam; and Chok Yaakov wrote that in our matter it is forbidden because of absorption, since there is some sharpness; and this too is forced, for Tur wrote stam that with water their sharpness is nullified; nevertheless for practical law it appears to be stringent, for Beit HaLevi in siman 69 and Peri Chadash resolved Taz's and Shach's difficulty that a vessel standing with gravy never loses its taste forever, only when empty it loses taste; and according to them Shulchan Aruch's words come for practical law according to their plain meaning; and so in Sefer Maamar Mordechai; and even though several Acharonim copied Taz's and Shach's words for halachah, nevertheless it does not appear to be lenient l'chatchila, especially here where Chok Yaakov also wrote for prohibition and Makor Chayim copied; however in time of pressure it appears one may rely to be lenient also in this, for otherwise Chok Yaakov's view above in sign 19 is not to forbid through pickling except in a vessel used frequently for chametz, when one must estimate against the whole; if not, we say there are sixty against its discharge — see there.
yad-ephraim/2:_: In Magen Avraham there subsection 2, and so it appears in siman 467 etc., and he did not distinguish whether the chicken is fat etc. — it should read: although Magen Avraham in siman 467 establishes that case with a weak one, for otherwise there is difficulty on the first view that does not hold to forbid all of it — see there; nevertheless his intent is not that he holds it deals only with a weak one alone, for this is a great forced reading to be so stam; but Per the first view he took cutting the place of permeation according to estimation, and if so he gave a general rule that everything is Per the matter of permeation; and in a weak chicken the matter of permeation is slight and removal suffices, and in a fat one that permeates through all by infusion, indeed it forbids all of it since the place of permeation is throughout; and on this are the differences of views afterward, that in every case even in a weak one it is forbidden because of turning the spit.
yad-ephraim/7:_: There subsection 15, and as he wrote siman 467 seif 14 etc. — meaning there in subsection 33 he wrote that if the brine does not rise above it, it has the law of salting, and its law as Rama wrote in his responsum — see there, Magen Avraham hinted here; and regarding that piece itself, what is outside the brine — one can also say it is permitted, as Taz wrote siman 467 subsection 20; and although in other prohibitions we say perhaps it permeates upward, nevertheless in chametz which is a weak prohibition one need not be stringent; and see in Shach siman 105; and more plausible that Magen Avraham refers to what was written above in the name of Rama regarding soaking overnight, and there the law of salting does not apply at all, for water nullifies the power of the brine, only from the law of pickling it is forbidden; and then what is outside the brine was not softened and did not absorb at all; and elsewhere I elaborated on this on Avodah Zarah at the beginning of siman 105 in the name of Or HaChaim, and what Magen Avraham wrote "and so Taz in Yoreh De'ah siman 83" — meaning there subsection 6, that we require the brine to rise above both of them, then it is like pickling when soaked overnight — see there; and what Magen Avraham wrote "and in Derishah siman 69 and in Beit Shmuel" etc., and in my humble opinion there is a missing word and it should read "and in Derishah siman 69 Derishah wrote that even for discharge from a vessel the law of pickling applies, and in Be'ur Sheva perek 25 Beit Shmuel wrote" etc., meaning Beit Shmuel holds the law of pickling does not help to discharge from a vessel; see Minchat Yaakov general rule 12 subsection 14.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: (2) [Levush] For we are accustomed to burn, etc. So Rama wrote in the name of Mordechai and rulings of Maharai siman 164; my brother-in-law in Chok Yaakov challenged: Mordechai refers to wheat not a chicken in which wheat was found; Maharai explained at length: if about wheat — why burn on Yom Tov; therefore explained it refers to less than kezayit no destruction needed — see there at length; and the challenge: Agudah on this Mordechai case wrote when he nullified it — therefore did not rule to burn on Yom Tov; and anyway Maharai's explanation is strained; rather plainly Maharai's explanation of the questioner: if to burn or cast in public domain; answered custom is burning; explained Mordechai's words; wrote on it "it does not appear he refers to the wheat itself" — regarding law for this he wrote even wheat needs no destruction for less than kezayit; if so it refers to custom and the same for the chicken; and so Agudah perek 2 of Pesachim explicitly we burn the chicken on chol hamoed — certainly Mordechai so explained; although Mordechai wrote chicken law in perek 2 — known Mordechai style; here he wrote in the name of R' Yehuda and below in other Poskim; and so in Amar Kol on parchment; and so Shibolei Leket end siman 63 and baraita — therefore do not deviate from Rama and Levush on this in any matter:
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: (3) [Levush] And the vessels retain, etc. Even if cooked in them a dish entirely chametz — only hide them in an unused room suffices; if mixed into a Yom Tov vessel Beit Chadash wrote: since some say chametz is also davar sheyesh lo matirin it is not nullified — end; and so She'erit Kenesset HaGedolah and Magen Avraham in his name; Chok Yaakov wrote there may be scribal error — must read "since some say vessel," etc. — not required; plainly for us chametz is not davar sheyesh lo matirin — nullified; however She'erit Kenesset HaGedolah gave another reason: Maharil and Ra'ah forbid also in other prohibitions in vessels; so Magen Avraham; in my book on Yoreh De'ah siman 102 I wondered on Maharil from Tosafot Bava Metzia daf 13 and Avodah Zarah daf 73 s.v. taval; and also even for Maharil earthenware where hagalah does not help are nullified — see there at length; Magen Avraham wrote on Pesach itself plainly forbidden — not better than other dry in dry; end; but She'erit Kenesset HaGedolah wrote they were not stringent to forbid dry in dry in any amount in the said vessels — absorbed minute amount nullifies; even absorption of full chametz be lenient when not ben yomo; nevertheless hide one vessel from them; what She'erit Kenesset HaGedolah challenged on Beit Chadash — his reason is also that chametz is davar sheyesh lo matirin — is wondrous; Beit Chadash wrote explicitly his reason is also chametz is davar sheyesh lo matirin as Shach siman 102 note 9:
eliyah-rabbah/7:_: (7) There are those who are lenient, etc. Shach in Yoreh De'ah siman 108 seized on Rama's "there are those who are lenient" and Darkei Moshe wrote so in Mordechai perek Kol Sha'ah; it is not in Mordechai — only reicha does not apply to chametz bread baked with matzah; but other dishes all agree there is prohibition — end; so Olat Shabbat; and he wondered on Rama — Mordechai wrote this in the name of Rabbenu Tam and he holds chametz on Pesach has no prohibition in any amount — end; in my humble opinion Darkei Moshe did not mean Rabbenu Tam's practice at all but the case Mordechai brought earlier — a gentile threw chametz cakes on Pesach into an oven and they ruled permitted because we hold reicha is not significant; if so proven he holds chametz equals other prohibitions — otherwise reicha would be significant and nevertheless permitted because there is no reicha in bread; and so explicitly in Rokeach siman 461 — otherwise what is the question from hadas of mitzvah forbidden to smell gentile incense; and Rabbenu Tam's case the distinction between bread seems clear he follows his view that in every prohibition reicha is significant as he wrote in Yoreh De'ah siman 97; therefore he needed a distinction of bread. For halachah Rama wrote in Yoreh De'ah there in loss rely on lenient; Beit Chadash is stringent here; what She'erit Kenesset HaGedolah wondered on Beit Chadash I already answered in Eliyahu Zuta; nevertheless since in responsum of Maharil siman 214 he wrote chametz equals other prohibitions and I also proved from Mordechai and Rokeach — be lenient in loss and Yom Tov joy; and it implies in Yoreh De'ah even in a small sealed oven; but large or small open permitted even without loss — unlike Olat Shabbat; and I also proved in my book on Yoreh De'ah Rama's view — what is lenient in loss is when slightly open where smoke exits; but completely sealed forbidden even in loss — so Magen Avraham; and I also wrote there Rashal forbids in other prohibitions even in loss when oven small and completely sealed — perhaps Maharil agrees. Rama wrote in Yoreh De'ah: if the prohibition is sharp and all the more if the permitted is sharp — forbidden even in loss; and implies even in open large oven as Torat Chatat wrote; although Rashal and Beit Chadash challenged — Taz and Shach wrote it is reasonable to forbid; in my book on Yoreh De'ah I wrote they did not analyze Mordechai perek Gid HaNasheh on roasted with spices — forbidden for it is sharp — end; seemingly wondrous why he did not write this general principle earlier that reicha is not significant — rather clear his explanation refers to what he wrote above that in large oven permitted; he wrote on it that in sharp forbidden; clear proof from responsum of Maharam Rotenburg siman 25 as I elaborated in my book. Sharp means most of the dish is sharp as Yoreh De'ah siman 122 seif 3. Rama wrote: if one is covered even in mere dough it is permitted — from Torat Chatat and Mordechai; in my book I proved from Mordechai and other Poskim dough covering does not help except for b'dieved permitted l'chatchila with dough; but in sharp forbidden unless bowl covering, etc.; all in roasting; in cooking permitted unless insulated for Shabbat all night sealed — so Magen Avraham; but implies he forbids chametz even in great loss — possibly lenient in great loss and Yom Tov joy. Incident before my ancestors the Gaon — they sealed the oven with food with a board used all year without rinsing and permitted. Forbidden to smell hot bread on Pesach — prohibition and permission siman 39:
biur-halacha/1:א: In any amount — see in Mishna Berurah what he wrote in the name of the Acharonim; and see in Peri Megadim who wrote that to sell to a gentile except the value of the prohibition therein — although we are accustomed to be stringent as Rama wrote in the gloss, nevertheless one may say that even where there is one side to be lenient it is permitted to sell to a gentile — see there:
biur-halacha/2:ב: And imparts taste for detriment, etc. — and likewise regarding reicha, all agree we are not stringent b'eyna like other prohibitions [Acharonim]:
biur-halacha/4:א: And was nullified in sixty — and likewise when there were not sixty but it imparted taste for detriment — and one should study: perhaps in this there is no dispute that it returns and revives, even per Rama in that siman it was only a general stringency concern for that view — see there. And know what the Mechaber wrote "and was nullified in sixty" — he gave the example of a moist thing nullified in sixty; and likewise a dry thing that became mixed, as Ateret Zekenim proved from responsum of Rashba siman 485. And even if nullified only one in two — so from Magen Avraham note 11 and it is plain; and those who disagree that it returns and revives — their view applies also to a moist thing that became mixed before Pesach and was nullified in sixty, as he wrote in siman 453 seif 3 in Mishna Berurah:
biur-halacha/4:ב: That it is moist, etc. — I did not copy what Taz wrote; it appears to me if moist became mixed in moist, etc. — many Poskim disagree on this as I wrote in siman 453 seif 3 — see there in Mishna Berurah:
biur-halacha/4:ד: Lest crumbs remained — although it is a doubt of a minute amount, nevertheless they were stringent because this doubt is close to certainty that presumably crumbs remained [see there]; and it appears plain that this law of Rama does not depend on the dispute of returns and revives — for even if we hold generally it does not return and revive, here it is forbidden as above in seif 3 while the wheat is still inside, for all forbid as Magen Avraham wrote there in note 8:
biur-halacha/8:ב: Permitted per all — meaning: although when they were not careful to cut with a new knife there is room to permit per some Poskim, nevertheless many forbid because they hold the sharpness of the olive spoils the absorbed taste and makes it for enhancement and they forbid; but when they were careful with the knife, even if they were not careful with the pot — one need not be concerned for a vessel not ben yomo because via the water in the pot its sharpness is nullified [Ma'amar Mordechai] — and plain:
biur-halacha/9:_: Dry in dry, etc. is not nullified — see in Peri Megadim in the introduction to this siman in Mishbetzot Zahav that one may permit to sell to a gentile except the value of the prohibition therein:
ateret-zekenim/3:_: Wheat found b'eyna, etc. — and likewise wheat found b'eyna in matzah is nullified in sixty even if not removed, provided it cooled before Pesach — permitted to eat the matzah cold and remove the wheat from there even on Pesach (Maharam Isserles and my teacher in Beit Chadash):
ateret-zekenim/5:_: Dry meat, etc. And in a wooden vessel — even though they salted in a chametz vessel, even ben yomo, it is permitted for we hold salting does not apply to wood. Salted meat and fish before Pesach — do not treat its prohibition lightly, meaning do not say stam vessels are not ben yomo and therefore when it is known the vessel is not ben yomo it is permitted even per Rosh; but from stam we are concerned the vessel was ben yomo — and so we practice ben yomo; and so Maharshal: we received from our ancestors not to soak salted meat — end of his words; however some practice leniency as written below siman 491 regarding dry cheese — some practice prohibition lest crumbs mixed in. And if already cooked those things — do not cast them to loss if impossible to keep until after Pesach; and all the more they do not forbid their mixture even in less than sixty, for it is only a rabbinic doubt of a minute amount; and if cut in a chametz knife Magen Avraham forbids even b'dieved — see there:
ateret-zekenim/9:_: Dry in dry, etc. — but if dry mixed in dry before Pesach — then its measure is a minute amount and its law is like other prohibitions as Mordechai wrote in perek Kol Sha'ah (see Beit Yosef); and if the chametz is a piece fit for honor or other things not nullified in other prohibitions — plainly so on Pesach too. Further in this seif dry in dry — however one may say specifically when mixed during Pesach; but if mixed before his Pesach they were nullified before Pesach and are permitted; and one may distinguish that here is different because the chametz body still exists — and even if mixed before Pesach perhaps forbidden — requires study; and cheese that was pickled, etc. — see below siman 491:
chatam-sofer/2:_: (There) in Magen Avraham beginning of siman and see in Yoreh De'ah siman 111 and Shach. Mishna Berurah: siman 102 in Shach note 13:
chatam-sofer/4:_: (There) in Magen Avraham note 4 wrote Semag: in every place see in Darkei Moshe Yoreh De'ah siman 35 note 7 [from the Gaon, may his memory be blessed]:
chatam-sofer/7:_: (There in Mechaber seif 4) it does not return and revive. Mishna Berurah: see responsa Chacham Tzvi Orach Chayim siman 107 [there he wrote to explain Mahari"v in responsum siman 214 and explain well]:
chatam-sofer/9:_: (In the said note) not like Shach. Mishna Berurah: siman 69 note 68:
chatam-sofer/10:_: (There in Magen Avraham note 23) Beit Yosef forbids because the matter is not placed upon him, etc. Mishna Berurah: see Shach Yoreh De'ah siman 94 note 28 and what Peri Megadim wrote there note 28:
chatam-sofer/11:_: (There in Magen Avraham note 24) and so Ran, Mishna Berurah: perek Kol Sha'ah daf 138 — see there:
chatam-sofer/12:_: (Taz in gloss seif 5) see in responsum Ahavah volume 1 siman 129 who brings from the Gaon Novi that he would protest that they take dye and their way is to buy it all year for tsekker and he had a tradition that it is chametz — see there in Turei Megadim; further the laws of types of tsekker [from the Gaon, may his memory be blessed]:
dagul-merevavah/3:_: In vain he was stringent: regarding discharging absorbed matter from a vessel — brine is also not pickling in less than twenty-four hours; and see Yoreh De'ah siman 79 in Shach note 68; and although Magen Avraham above note 15 concludes in this not like Shach — nevertheless in vinegar which anyway is not like brine one may be lenient:
eshel-avraham/1:ב: Regarding a cooked dish — see responsum Yoreh De'ah siman 222:
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (2) And Zohar wrote in parashat Ki Teitzei daf 282b: and thus — on the night of guarding all need to be guarded from chametz and se'or in any amount and all foods and drinks are guarded; whoever guards them from chametz and se'or — he is guarded from the evil inclination below and the soul above; and it is said of him: evil shall not dwell with you, for his body became holy and his soul holy of holies; and it is said of the evil inclination and any stranger shall not eat holy, and the stranger who approaches shall die — end of his words. Beit Ahron wrote so in the name of the Ari, may his memory be blessed; and now I did not find it:
kaf-hachayyim/9:_: (9) Wheat found in a pot — the spoon with which they stirred the pot is forbidden; if they stirred other pots with it — all are forbidden. Tur siman 467. Chayei Adam there. And so Ateret Zekenim in this siman end of letter 1: the spoon that absorbed from a minute amount forbids in a minute amount. And although in a piece forbidden in a minute amount Ateret Zekenim holds it does not return and forbid in a minute amount as in the previous letter — he already wrote there the reason: specifically from a piece the minute amount cannot spread; but from a spoon that has no taste of its own it can spread — see there; meaning when the piece has taste, when it discharges, etc.:
netiv-chayim/11:_: (Magen Avraham note 38) the words of Shach in Yoreh De'ah siman 96 note 26 and Beit Chadash here seif 3 — so it should read:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/10:_: Seif 4 — it does not return and revive on Pesach; see in Magen Avraham siman 466 note 8; in siman 467 in Taz note 18:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/11:_: In the gloss — we are concerned lest crumbs remained; and although there are sixty rabbinically, nevertheless we are concerned for it is common that it crumbles — so he wrote above; and in my opinion per Magen Avraham: if they strained before Pesach it would help that taste for detriment applies — one may say therefore its doubt is forbidden because it is something that imparts taste; for although we hold chametz is not something that imparts taste — since permitted b'eyna in sixty — see Magen Avraham note 40: meaning it returns and becomes forbidden; but regarding Pesach afterward one need not rely on sixty — for even if crumbs remain it is permitted because taste for detriment applies; if so relative to sixty it is called something that imparts taste — requires study:
shaarei-teshuvah/8:_: Prohibitions — see Beit HaTov; and see in responsum Mishna Berurah part 1 siman 21: at the fifth hour nokshah is permitted per all; and per those who hold nokshah is rabbinic — permitted b'eyna all day — see there; however many Poskim who hold nokshah is Torah forbid nokshah from the fifth hour onward; and see in responsum Beit Efrayim siman 30; and see in Mishna Berurah Ma'amar Torah: although nokshah is rabbinic — do not permit selling to a gentile when the dish lacks sixty against chametz nokshah as with full chametz, even if there are sixty — see there:
shaarei-teshuvah/12:_: And revives — see Beit HaTov; and see in Tiferet Tzvi: wheat cooked in a dish b'eyna and cooled before night and remained pickled ma'al lema'alah during Pesach days — the wheat discharges also afterward via pickling and forbids — see there; and see below siman 467 what he wrote in the name of the place of Shmuel regarding pickling and doubt whether it split — see there:
yad-ephraim/8:_: There note 16: salt does not discharge at all what is absorbed in the vessel — it is as if, etc. — so it should read:
